messages:
julia_support: FYI support ticket from acme-inc: they report repeated 5xx / 504 gateway timeouts and very high tail latency hitting hosted API since ~11:07 UTC. customer id acme-123. examples: req=req_1a2b3c (504), req=req_4d5e6f (502). p95 ~8s, p99 ~22s.

mike_oncall: oncall here, assigning. can you paste the curl request they used + any sampling logs? also their tenant throughput (rps) and quota? @ingress-bot pull qdepth metrics for acme-123 from 10:50-11:20 UTC.

julia_support: curl they used: ```curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rw-1-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize the dataset"}],"max_tokens":256}'```
They were sending bursty parallel requests from a batch job ~120rps for a 30s window, usually low steady-state <5rps. Attached sample gateway logs: ``[11:08:11] ingress: enqueue tenant=acme-123 qdepth=980 req=req_1a2b3c`` and ``[11:08:41] backend: dispatch timeout -> 504 req=req_1a2b3c``

ingress-bot: metrics pulled: queue_depth(acme-123) peaked at 986 at 11:08:12. continuous-batcher backlog length increased concurrently. avg batch latency climbed from 40ms -> 480ms.

sahil_runtime: initial hypothesis: continuous batching backlog + queue depth limit hit causing long wait and eventual gateway deadline. likely a mix of tenant burst + big max_batch_size + batching window that grows backlog. Did they use rw-1-large (longer decode times)?

julia_support: yes model rw-1-large. customer confirmed they ramped to warm parallelism for a data migration.

anya_ops: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) soft-throttle tenant at the gateway (limit to 20rps) 2) temporarily reduce max_batch_size for hosted pool from 32 -> 8 for this tenant or pool 3) reduce batch_window_ms small (50ms) to flush smaller batches faster. Which should we do first?

mike_oncall: do soft-throttle first to stop tailing. @ops-lead can you apply tenant rate limit for acme-123 now? then change batching config if we still see p99 high.

ops-lead: applying throttle: `POST /admin/tenants/acme-123/rate_limit {"rps":20}` -> applied at 11:12:05 UTC :white_check_mark:. Notifying customer via support.

julia_support: customer notified and asked to pause migration for 10m. They paused.

mike_oncall: while throttle is in place, we'll also patch runtime to reduce `max_batch_size` for rw-1-large in hosted pool to 8 and lower `batch_window_ms` to 40ms for high-q tenants. @sahil_runtime can you stage a rollout? keep it small (single region) first.

sahil_runtime: creating change. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/changes/PR-8423 (staged config change). Will rollout to us-west-2 pool at 11:18 UTC canary.

ingress-bot: canary started @11:18:45, target hosts=6, traffic cutover 5%.

sahil_runtime: canary looks good for 2m. batch size reduced, batch latency p50->70ms, p99 dropped from 22s -> 1.9s in canary hosts. I'll promote to full region at 11:22 UTC.

ops-lead: promoted to all hosts in us-west-2 at 11:22:15.

mike_oncall: metrics after change + throttle: queue_depth peak dropped to 120, p95 ~900ms, p99 ~1.9s, 504 count fell to zero in the last 3m. rolling observed improvement.

customer_success: customer confirmed they see reduced 504s and are continuing ramp slowly. asked for recommended config for future migrations.

julia_support: provided guidance: use rate-limited ramp, use dedicated capacity for sustained bursts, or contact AE to onboard dedicated pool. Also recommended smaller model or lower concurrency for short windows.

mike_oncall: action items: - open incident ticket INC-2026-3456 (created) - follow-up PR to add tenant-aware adaptive batching (sahil) - runbook update: add a section for rapid tenant throttling and config keys (julia/anya) - notify product about UX for 'emergency throttle' (customer-success).

sahil_runtime: started follow-up ticket: #RT-723 add tenant-adaptive-batching experiment.

anya_ops: will add a grafana panel for per-tenant queue_depth and continuous-batcher backlog; ETA EOD.

julia_support: marking support ticket as "monitoring" and will keep customer updated. closing immediate escalation. thanks all :tada:

mike_oncall: oncall note: if we see similar spikes, preferred order = 1) tenant soft-throttle 2) reduce batching window / max_batch_size 3) route to dedicated pool. tagging this thread into the incident.

julia_support: final: last observed 504 at 11:11:58, none after mitigations. will reopen if symptoms return.
